subject: Computer Networking
title: MIME and Attachments
description: A quick, practical guide to MIME and Attachments.

hook.text: Email was designed for plain text. MIME is the hack that lets you send images, PDFs, and HTML.

buildup.text: MIME — Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions — wraps non-text content with type labels and encoding.

discovery.text: Base64 encoding converts binary files to ASCII text. The receiver decodes it back to the original file.

twist.text: A single email can have multiple MIME parts: plain text, HTML version, and attachments side by side.

climax.text: Content-Type headers tell the client what each part is: text/plain, image/png, application/pdf.

punchline.text: MIME makes email multimedia. Text protocol, rich content.

quiz.question: What encoding does MIME use to send binary files as text?

details.summary: MIME extends email beyond plain text to support attachments, images, HTML formatting, and multiple character sets. It encodes binary files as text using Base64 so they can travel through text-only SMTP servers. Every email attachment you send uses MIME encoding.
details.whyItMatters: Without MIME, email could only carry plain ASCII text. MIME made email a rich communication medium supporting any file type, formatting, and language.
takeaways: MIME enables attachments, HTML formatting, and character sets
Binary files are encoded as text using Base64 for SMTP transport
MIME types identify the content type of each message part

faq.question: Why do attachments make emails so much larger?
faq.answer: Base64 encoding converts binary data to text characters, increasing size by about 33 percent. A 3 MB photo becomes roughly 4 MB in the email. This overhead exists because SMTP was designed for text only, and MIME must encode binary data as text for transport.

faq.question: What are MIME types used for?
faq.answer: MIME types tell the receiving client what each part of the email contains: text/plain for text, image/jpeg for photos, application/pdf for PDFs. The client uses this to decide how to display or handle each part. Web servers also use MIME types for HTTP responses.
